learningObjectives.title: Density and the kinetic theory of matter

questions.q: Which equation correctly defines the density of a material?
questions.explain: Density is defined as the mass of a substance divided by its volume (ρ = m/V).

questions.q: What is the SI unit of density?
questions.explain: Density is mass per unit volume, so its SI unit is kilograms per cubic metre (kg/m³).

questions.q: What is the approximate density of pure water?
questions.explain: Water has a density of 1000 kg/m³, equivalent to 1 g/cm³.

questions.q: A metal block has a mass of 240 g and a volume of 30 cm³. What is its density?
questions.explain: Density = mass ÷ volume = 240 ÷ 30 = 8 g/cm³.

questions.q: Rearranging the density equation, how is mass calculated from density and volume?
questions.explain: Rearranging ρ = m/V gives m = ρ × V.

questions.q: What is the best way to measure the volume of a small, irregularly shaped stone?
options: Lower it into a measuring cylinder of water and record the water displaced
Measure its length, width and height with a ruler
Weigh it on a top-pan balance
Time how long it takes to fall
questions.explain: The volume of an irregular solid equals the volume of water it displaces.

questions.q: An object has a mass of 500 g and a density of 2.5 g/cm³. What is its volume?
questions.explain: Volume = mass ÷ density = 500 ÷ 2.5 = 200 cm³.

questions.q: According to kinetic theory, how are the particles arranged in a solid?
options: Closely packed in a regular, fixed pattern
Far apart and moving randomly at high speed
Close together but able to move past one another
Spread out with large gaps and no attraction
questions.explain: In a solid the particles are tightly packed in a fixed, regular arrangement and can only vibrate.

questions.q: Why is a gas normally much less dense than a solid of the same substance?
options: Its particles are spread far apart, so there is more empty space per unit volume
Its particles are packed more tightly together
questions.explain: In a gas the same particles occupy a much larger volume, giving a far lower mass per unit volume.

questions.q: When a solid melts to become a liquid, what happens to its particles?
options: They gain energy and can move past one another while staying close together
They lose energy and stop moving completely
They move far apart with large gaps between them
They are destroyed and reform as new particles
questions.explain: On melting, particles gain enough energy to break their fixed positions and flow, but remain close together.

questions.q: Which equation gives the pressure exerted by a force acting on a surface?
questions.explain: Pressure is the force acting per unit area (p = F/A).

questions.q: What is the unit of pressure?
questions.explain: Pressure is measured in pascals, where 1 Pa = 1 N/m².

questions.q: Why do wide snowshoes stop a walker sinking into soft snow?
options: The larger area spreads the weight, reducing the pressure on the snow
The larger area increases the pressure on the snow
They increase the force on the snow
questions.explain: For the same force, a larger contact area gives a smaller pressure, so the snow is less likely to give way.

questions.q: A force of 200 N acts on an area of 4 m². What pressure is exerted?
questions.explain: Pressure = force ÷ area = 200 ÷ 4 = 50 Pa.

questions.q: A person wearing narrow high-heeled shoes can dent a soft floor more than when wearing flat shoes. Why?
options: The small contact area of the heel produces a much higher pressure
The heel produces a much larger force on the floor
The small area produces a much lower pressure
The person's weight increases when wearing heels
questions.explain: The same weight acting over a very small area gives a very high pressure, denting the floor.

questions.q: Why does a sharp knife cut more easily than a blunt one?
options: Its thin edge has a small area, giving a high pressure for the same force
Its thin edge produces a larger force
Its thin edge spreads the force over a large area
A sharp knife has a greater weight
questions.explain: A small contact area concentrates the force into a high pressure, making it easier to cut.

questions.q: Which equation gives the pressure at a depth in a liquid?
options: pressure = density × gravitational field strength × depth
questions.explain: The pressure in a column of liquid is p = ρgh, where h is the depth.

questions.q: Why is a dam built much thicker at its base than at its top?
options: Water pressure increases with depth, so the base must withstand a greater pressure
Water pressure decreases with depth, so the base needs less support
The pressure is the same everywhere, but the base looks better thicker
The top experiences the greatest water pressure
questions.explain: Pressure in a liquid increases with depth (p = ρgh), so the deeper base must be stronger.

questions.q: What is the pressure due to water at a depth of 2 m? (density of water = 1000 kg/m³, g = 10 N/kg)
How does the pressure in a liquid act at a given depth?
options: Only sideways towards the container walls
questions.explain: At a given depth a liquid exerts the same pressure in all directions.
